analysis: All supplied changes are documentation and a changelog. No executable source is in this batch, so no code-level regression can be shown from this evidence. The docs describe hardening of the add-on hold (TB-012, A-018, T-059). Four behaviors are described: (1) a model load already running when a hold starts ends with a retryable 503, and the hold reports `held` only after the load gate is free (addon-hold.md head lines 90-93); (2) the drain-bound cancellation stops on release and cancels only requests it found running (lines 94-96); (3) the add-on socket verifies the peer signer before a connection takes one of 8 slots, with a 10 s request-line deadline, and the hold record and mailbox files are read without blocking so a FIFO is refused (changelog lines 11-15); (4) `loaded-models.json` is not rewritten while a hold is active. Each is a defensive improvement that narrows T-059 DoS exposure. The docs also note that a load still running after the 60 s settle timeout is waited for until it unwinds, so a stuck load could keep the hold in `draining`. That is a documented availability trade-off, not a new security gap. The new link to security/local-control.md is not supplied, so its trust-boundary claims are unverified. The implementing Swift sources (ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift, AddonIPCServer.swift, AddonHoldStore.swift, ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift, ProviderLoop+StartupPreload.swift, ProviderLoop+NativeMiMo.swift) are not supplied. The code must be reviewed to confirm the checks match the docs: the load-gate fence on every load path, peer verification before slot allocation, O_NONBLOCK/no-follow regular-file opens, and the persistLoadedModelSet suppression. The inference.md excerpt is truncated, so the full table row was not seen.
